newsitem.title: BENIN: Strike paralyses Benin's Cotonou port.
newsitem.headline: Strike paralyses Benin's Cotonou port.

text.p: Office workers paralysed Benin's main port of Cotonou on Monday with a lightning one-day strike over government plans to replace their managing director and his team, witnesses and union officials said.

Up to 400 members of the national union of the port of Cotonou SYNTRAPAC, who accuse the government of politicising the port, stopped dockers going to work there and servicing six ships including fuel tankers and container vessels.
Cotonou port, which serves landlocked Niger, Burkina Faso, Mali and even neighbouring Nigeria, is a major source of revenue for the West African nation's economy.

The government of Mathieu Kerekou, the former Marxist military leader who returned to power through the ballot box in March 1996, has called for the replacement of the state-owned port authority's managing director Issa Badarou-Soule and his team before the end of April.
"This is a politicisation of the port and a vendetta which has suicidal consequences for the company," SYNTRAPAC general-secretary Francis Kpanou told reporters.
The move followed a report from a parliamentary commission of inquiry on the administration of the port.
Kerekou's predecessor, Nicephore Soglo, appointed Badarou.
